name: MIRIX
one_line: Letta-derived multi-agent memory server: a meta memory manager LLM routes each input batch to up to five typed memory-manager agents (core, episodic, semantic, resource, knowledge vault; procedural is produced by a separate skill-distillation path), stored in PostgreSQL with BM25 and pgvector, read via LLM topic extraction then per-type retrieval.

locomo.protocol: Paper Table 2: gpt-4.1-mini backbone (write agents and reader), GPT-4.1 LLM judge, adversarial category excluded (cat 1-4, 1,540 q), mean of 3 runs (83.98 / 87.34 / 84.82); per category single-hop 85.11, multi-hop 83.70, open-domain 65.62, temporal 88.39; Full-Context 87.52 under same setup
locomo.source: MIRIX paper arXiv 2507.07957, Section 4.3, Table 2 and Appendix A Table 3

locomo.protocol: Vendor graph-revision branch PR #123: LLM judge on 1,540 q; reader/judge not stated in PR body; baseline 0.5429 for the then-current MIRIX, 0.5734 with MIRIX_ENABLE_GRAPH_MEMORY on
locomo.source: github.com/Mirix-AI/MIRIX/pull/123 body (merged into graph-revision branch, not main)

arch.product.t: Self-hosted FastAPI server (port 8531) plus React dashboard and Python SDK (mirix-client); three tiers client SDK -> REST -> AsyncServer -> MetaAgent with typed sub-agents. Forked from Letta (agent loop, blocks, tool execution). The screen-capture desktop app from the paper is not in this repo.

arch.truth.t: Derived typed rows are the de facto truth: raw turns are not kept for retrieval by default. Raw turns are persisted to a Conversation Message Store only when a session_id is supplied (used solely for skill distillation); agent in-context messages are cleared after each memory update (CLEAR_HISTORY_AFTER_MEMORY_UPDATE=true).

arch.stores.t: PostgreSQL + pgvector (one table per memory type: block, episodic_memory, semantic_memory, procedural_memory, resource_memory, knowledge_vault, plus raw_memory, conversation_message, skill_experience); optional Redis Stack as search cache (MIRIX_REDIS_ENABLED default false); SQLite fallback.

arch.graphdb.t: No graph store on main. A temporal knowledge graph (entity_nodes, entity_edges, episode_nodes, involves_edges; default off) exists only on the graph-revision / graph_v7.1_clean branches.
arch.graphdb.e: grep for neo4j/entity_node in mirix/ returns nothing [read]; PR #123 body [doc]

arch.scope.t: Organisation -> client (API key) -> user; every row carries organization_id, user_id, client_id and a filter_tags JSON with scope = client.write_scope; reads filter by client.read_scopes plus arbitrary filter_tags (GIN-indexed).

write.entry.t: POST /memory/add (queued) and POST /memory/add_sync (blocking); messages are role-prefixed text ([USER]/[ASSISTANT]/[TOOL]); optional session_id, session_tag (conversation|task), occurred_at, filter_tags, chaining flag. Also POST /memory/raw for unprocessed task context.

write.receipt.t: /memory/add returns status 'queued' after put_messages; default queue is an in-process asyncio memory queue (QUEUE_TYPE=memory, 1 worker), so a crash loses unprocessed batches. Kafka (protobuf or JSON, mTLS) is opt-in. Only the optional Conversation Message Store write is durable before return.

write.roles.t: All roles go to the meta memory manager as one prefixed text blob; the LLM decides what to keep. Episodic rows carry an 'actor' field (user or assistant). session_tag='task' suppresses all inline extraction (skill-only); 'conversation' never feeds skills.

write.firewall.t: not found: no injection or poisoning filter on the write path; the meta prompt even asks agents to over-include memory types when unsure.

write.governance.t: Knowledge Vault deliberately stores credentials (prompt example: a WiFi password) with a sensitivity label; 'high' items are hidden from non-vault agents' prompts but secret_value is a plain String column (no encryption found). Raw task memories have a 14-day TTL via a cron job. No consent or redaction.
write.governance.e: mirix/orm/knowledge_vault.py:72-78 [read]; mirix/agent/agent.py:1844-1870 [read]; mirix/jobs/cleanup_raw_memories.py:4-37 [read]; grep 'encrypt' finds nothing relevant [read]

segment.unit.t: One call to /memory/add = one batch; the whole batch is one meta-agent step. The paper app accumulates 20 inputs (TEMPORARY_MESSAGE_LIMIT) before absorbing; the LoCoMo harness sends one full session per add.

segment.rule.t: Caller-defined; no server-side boundary detection. Episodic agent itself chooses insert (new topic) versus merge (same topic continues) per batch. MAB harness uses a 4,096-token sentence-aware chunker.

segment.measured.t: not found: per-session add timings are logged by the harness but no published counts of calls or units on LoCoMo.

extract.calls.t: Per batch: 1 topic-extraction call (meta agent, step 0) + 1 meta-manager call choosing memory types + 1 call per selected sub-agent run concurrently via asyncio.gather (up to 5), more if chaining is on. With chaining=False (LoCoMo harness) roughly 3-7 LLM calls per session. Paper: 'one to the meta memory manager and between zero and six to the other memory managers'.

extract.facts.t: Semantic memory holds concept/person/place entries (name, summary, details, source), not atomic facts; Knowledge Vault holds static reference values (caption + secret_value).

extract.episode.t: Episodic events with event_type, summary, verbose details, actor, occurred_at; the agent is told to make one comprehensive call per batch and to merge into an existing event when the topic continues.

extract.dates.t: occurred_at is LLM-produced per event unless the API occurred_at override is passed; the LoCoMo harness prepends instructions to resolve relative dates ('last year' -> 2022) into the text, so absolute dates are prompt-driven, not code-driven.

extract.neighbours.t: Each sub-agent's system prompt is rebuilt with retrieved memories for the batch topics: its own type with row IDs (for merge/replace) and other types without IDs, MAX_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT_IN_SYSTEM=10 per list (prompt text still says 50). Episodic entries show summary plus details length only.

extract.failure.t: Tool failure injects a 'function call failed' heartbeat and lets the agent retry (chaining); one failing sub-agent raises RuntimeError for the whole trigger_memory_update. Context overflow triggers up to 3 summariser retries. Queue has no dead-letter in memory mode.

graph.entities.t: No entity extraction on main; semantic-memory entries named after people/places act as implicit entity cards.

graph.resolution.t: not found on main (semantic dedup is exact name+summary+details equality).

graph.edges.t: not found on main; edges only on graph-revision branch.

time.fields.t: Episodic occurred_at plus created_at and last_modify {timestamp, operation}; other types have created_at/last_modify only. No valid-from/valid-to.

time.update.t: LLM-driven destructive edits: episodic merge overwrites summary/details; replace deletes rows and inserts new ones; semantic/resource/vault update tools overwrite. No history kept beyond last_modify. Auto-dream (POST /memory/auto_dream, operator- or schedule-invoked) resolves stale/conflicting entries.

time.dedup.t: Semantic insert skips exact duplicates among up to 1,000 existing items; the meta agent's duplicate memory_types are de-duplicated; otherwise dedup relies on the LLM and on auto-dream consolidation.

derive.session.t: not found as a stored layer; agents' own in-context histories are summarised at 75% context pressure (keep last 5 messages), which is working-memory hygiene, not a retrievable summary.

derive.profile.t: Core memory blocks 'human' and 'persona' (5,000-char limit each) maintained by the core memory agent with append/rewrite tools; overflow returns an error telling the agent to condense to about 50%. Always injected whole into every agent prompt.

derive.entity.t: Semantic memory entries about people/organisations serve as entity summaries (no dedicated layer).

derive.background.t: Auto-dream consolidation agent per mode (core/episodic/semantic/resource/procedural/knowledge/experience, up to 500 items per type, advisory-locked); procedural mode is auto-scheduled every 5 'task' sessions (SKILL_TRIGGER_SESSION_THRESHOLD); others are invoked by API. Reflexion and background agents exist but are off (WITH_REFLEXION_AGENT=False).

derive.forget.t: No decay scoring. Raw task memories hard-deleted after 14 days by a nightly job; otherwise deletion only via LLM replace tools, auto-dream, or API.

index.embed.t: Configurable per agent (README example Google text-embedding-004, 768-d; eval config OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 1536-d); vectors zero-padded to MAX_EMBEDDING_DIM=4096. Episodic insert embeds both details and summary (2 embedding calls per event). BUILD_EMBEDDINGS_FOR_MEMORY can switch embedding off.

index.lexical.t: PostgreSQL to_tsvector('english') GIN indexes on summary, details and combined; ranking ts_rank_cd with AND query first, OR fallback for recall; Redis Search text index when cache on; in-memory rank_bm25 on SQLite.

index.vector.t: pgvector columns per text field (episodic details/summary; semantic name/summary/details; vault caption); no ANN index declared (GIN only), so vector search is a scan; 4,096-d padding exceeds pgvector's HNSW dimension cap (inferred). Redis vector index when cache on.

read.rewrite.t: Active retrieval: an LLM call with forced tool update_topic_and_time turns the conversation into ';'-separated topics plus a temporal phrase; topics become the BM25 query. Optional local Ollama model for topic extraction (no temporal).

read.analysis.t: Temporal expression parsed by a rule-based parser (today, yesterday, last week ...) into a date range relative to the user's timezone; explicit start/end dates override.

read.legs.t: /memory/retrieve/conversation: per type, BM25 only (search_method hard-coded 'bm25'), limit 10 per type: episodic recent + relevant, semantic, resource, procedural, knowledge vault captions, plus all core blocks; run sequentially. /memory/search defaults to embedding (procedural: hybrid BM25+embedding RRF k=60) and runs all types concurrently.

read.temporal.t: Date range filter on episodic occurred_at only (other types unfiltered).

rank.fusion.t: No cross-type fusion: results stay grouped per memory type. Within procedural, RRF (k=60) fuses BM25 and embedding.

rank.gate.t: Optional similarity_threshold on embedding search; the memory prompt tells the model that empty sections mean no relevant memory. No abstain gate.

rank.agentic.t: Chat agent has search_in_memory / list_memory_within_timerange tools; the LoCoMo harness answer agent (gpt-4.1-mini) gets the preliminary retrieval then up to 5 search_memory rounds (default embedding, limit raised to 15).

answer.shape.t: Typed XML sections in the system prompt: current time, <keywords>, <core_memory>, <episodic_memory> recent and relevant (timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)'), <knowledge_vault>, <semantic_memory>, <resource_memory>, each with 'k out of N items'; procedural never injected. LoCoMo harness flattens summaries/captions with timestamps into one block.

answer.size.t: not found: no published tokens per question. Bounded by design at about 50-60 short lines (10 per list) plus up to 10,000 chars of core blocks (inferred).

answer.prompt.t: Harness answer agent is told to verify results, search both episodic and semantic, aggregate lists, stop after 2-3 searches, and only say 'unknown' after three failed searches.

eval.best.t: 85.38 LoCoMo (cat 1-4), vendor paper, gpt-4.1-mini, mean of 3 runs, below its own Full-Context 87.52. The vendor's own later branch run reports 54.29 -> 57.34 on 1,540 q, far below the paper.

eval.outside.t: No independent reproduction found in repo or paper; the task note attributes an 85.38 run to the HyperMem authors, which could not be verified here (same number as the vendor paper, so probably a citation, not a rerun).

eval.models.t: Paper: gpt-4.1-mini writer and reader, GPT-4.1 judge. Repo harness: gpt-4.1-mini memory agents, gpt-4.1-nano topic extraction, text-embedding-3-small, gpt-4.1-mini answer agent, gpt-4o-mini judge (generous Mem0-style prompt). Judges differ between paper and repo.

eval.rigour.t: 3 runs reported with per-run spread (83.98-87.34); baselines run once and re-implemented; harness injects date-resolution instructions into each ingested session and lets the reader do up to 5 agentic searches; cat 5 dropped (no 'answer' key, skipped).

cost.write.t: About 3-7 LLM calls per session with chaining off: roughly 800-1,900 calls for 272 sessions, plus 2 embedding calls per episodic event and more per semantic/vault row (inferred from code path); each call carries a 650-1,300-word agent prompt plus retrieved memory lists.
cost.write.e: mirix/agent/agent.py:1657-1699 [read]; memory_tools.py:1995-2012 [read]; prompt word counts via wc [read]; inferred

cost.read.t: 1 topic-extraction LLM call per /retrieve/conversation plus DB queries (BM25); harness adds 1-6 answer-agent calls with search rounds.

cost.where.t: Hosted LLMs by default (OpenAI, Gemini, Anthropic, Azure etc. via llm_api); optional local Ollama for topic extraction only.

trust.provenance.t: Rows record agent_id, client_id, user_id, filter_tags (scope, session_id, session_tag), last_modify operation; semantic/vault have a free-text 'source'. No link from a derived row to source turns or message IDs.

trust.erasure.t: DELETE /users/{user_id}/memories hard-deletes memories, messages and blocks for a user and clears Redis keys; per-item deletes per type; per-client delete.

trust.auth.t: X-API-Key (SHA-256 hashed at rest) or dashboard JWT; client context via x-client-id / x-org-id headers.

trust.sharing.t: Scopes let multiple clients write to their write_scope and read a list of read_scopes for the same user; agents inside a meta agent share one store. Gaps: the retrieve path queries knowledge_vault without filter_tags/scopes, and agent-prompt retrieval passes no scopes.

extras.t: One LLM call classifies each batch into memory types and fans out to typed manager agents concurrently (asyncio.gather), each with a narrow toolset and type-specific prompt.
'task' sessions skip all inline extraction and only feed skill distillation every 5 sessions; 'conversation' sessions never produce skills.

Procedural memory as versioned skills (name, description, instructions, triggers, examples, version) with an edit budget and size gates; sealed sessions distilled into worth_learning / worth_avoiding experiences that evolve skills.
Offline agent reviews one or more memory types, merges duplicates and resolves stale entries; dry_run supported.

Screen-monitor prompt set and a TemporaryMessageAccumulator (20 inputs, async Gemini file upload, image cleanup) exist, but the accumulator is not wired into the server; the paper's 1 fps screenshot app with >0.99 similarity skip is outside this repo.
Optional Redis Stack mirror with text and vector indexes queried before PostgreSQL; 1-hour TTL.
Opt-in Kafka transport (protobuf or JSON, mTLS) with user_id-hash partitioned workers.
MCP tool registry/marketplace and sandboxed user-defined tools for the chat agent.

token_economy.t: Four mechanisms: (1) topic extraction compresses the conversation to a short ';'-separated keyword string before retrieval; (2) each typed list is capped at 10 items (MAX_RETRIEVAL_LIMIT_IN_SYSTEM) and episodic rows are shown as timestamp + summary + '(Details: N Characters)', so verbose details are fetched only on demand; (3) procedural skills are never broadcast into prompts, only fetched by search; (4) memory agents' chat history is wiped after each update and agent context is summarised at 75% pressure down to 10% (keep last 5). Core blocks are capped at 5,000 chars each and always injected. Paper storage claim: 15.89 MB SQLite versus 15.07 GB raw screenshots (99.9% less). No tokens-per-question figure published.

speed.t: Async-native stack (asyncpg, redis.asyncio, aiokafka, httpx). Write is queued and returns immediately; sub-agents for different memory types run concurrently; worker pool partitioned by user_id hash (default 1 worker). /memory/search over all types runs concurrently and embeds the query once; /memory/retrieve/conversation is sequential and BM25-only. Optional Redis cache. Paper uses Gemini for async image upload. No latency numbers published; the harness records add/answer timings locally.

keep: A cheap router call that picks which typed extractors run per batch, then runs them in parallel with small type-specific prompts and toolsets.
Active retrieval: one small-model call that outputs topics plus a temporal phrase, the phrase resolved to a date range by a rule-based parser, not the LLM.
Pointer-style context: show a summary plus details length, keep IDs only for the owning writer, and fetch details on demand.
Skills as a retrieval target, not ambient context, plus routing of task versus conversation sessions to different consolidation paths.
Neighbour-aware writes: each extractor sees the top-k existing rows of its own type with IDs, so it can merge or replace instead of appending.
avoid: Destructive LLM merges and replaces with no version history or link back to source turns; raw turns are not kept by default, so errors cannot be audited or re-derived.
Knowledge Vault stores credentials in a plain-text column, and the retrieve path queries it without scope filters.
Queued /memory/add returns before durability (in-process queue by default), and one failing sub-agent fails the whole fan-out.
Paper 85.38 (gpt-4.1-mini, GPT-4.1 judge, agentic reader) is not reproduced by the vendor's later 1,540-q branch run (54.29-57.34); the 4,096-d padding blocks ANN indexing.
